title: Compact Request Synthesis Canvas — lightweight drill-down for tracing & cost
creator: Arianna Lowe
description: Problem: Engineers frequently need a fast, low-friction way to understand a single request end-to-end (spans, correlation IDs, timeline) while also seeing token-level cost signals and rollout/model variant context. Existing heavy trace inspectors support deep analysis but are slow to open, take up screen real estate, and interrupt developer flow. Goal: design a Compact Request Synthesis Canvas (CRSC) — a lightweight, horizontal canvas that surfaces the essential request summary, a concise span timeline, correlation metadata, quick-filters, and inline cost annotations. The canvas should be usable as a slide-over from any dashboard row and as an inline expansion in the request list. Key constraints: must fit comfortably in 420-720px widths, render within 150ms on initial open (prototype target), avoid duplicating full trace detail UIs, and integrate with rollouts/canary metadata for model selection. Out of scope: full trace replay UI, deep span heatmaps, or long-form flamegraphs (those remain in full inspector). Primary users: SREs debugging latency anomalies, Platform engineers triaging cost regressions, and PMs reviewing rollout impacts. Success metrics: reduced time-to-first-insight (TTFI) by 30% for common triage flows and fewer full-inspector opens for low-friction investigations.
updates: 2026-02-28 - Kickoff: scoped with PM and Eng (Priya Kapoor, Daniel Ruiz). Aligned on compact canvas goals and constraints. Decided canvas will be accessible from request list and dashboard row actions.
2026-03-03 - Exploratory sketches and 3 layout directions produced. Direction A (card + mini-timeline) chosen for technical feasibility. Sketches uploaded to Figma.
2026-03-05 - Prototype: interactive Figma prototype with timeline scrub, span preview tooltip, and cost badges. Link added to design_links. Usability research plan drafted for 4 internal sessions.

2026-03-07 - Eng review with runtime team: confirmed ability to supply compact payload (summary + first 6 spans + kv headers + cost delta) via new endpoint. ENG suggested adding precomputed cost_delta field to avoid client-side aggregation.
2026-03-09 - PM feedback: request that canvas surface rollout/model info and a quick "fallbacks" indicator when runtime used a lower-cost variant. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-11 - Design review: iterated on contrast and microcopy for correlation IDs, added copy to clarify privacy/PII handling. Minor accessibility fixes applied to color tokens and focus states.
2026-03-12 - Prototype handoff prep: created component spec for Console Design System; added engineering implementation notes and an initial storybook stub in the design_links.
Next steps: run 4 internal usability sessions (week of 2026-03-15), finalize engineering payload shape with ENG-4512, and begin a small pilot A/B in console-2026.04 release.

acceptance_criteria: Canvas opens as a slide-over and inline-expansion from request rows without blocking full inspector.
Shows request summary (id, start/end, status), top-level tags, and first 6 spans with short names and duration bars.
Inline token-level cost badges appear on spans when available and show delta vs baseline model.
Correlation ID is copyable, clickable (opens full inspector), and surfaces related requests count.
Contains quick filters for trace-level severity (error/warn), latency buckets, and cost delta thresholds.
Accessible keyboard navigation and meets AA contrast for text and badges.
Engineers can retrieve canvas data via a single compact endpoint (payload ≤ 8KB typical).
